aka: ZHX / ZFHX / HOMEZ / TSHZ / HMBOX / HHEX group
short: This family collects homeodomains that do not behave like homeodomains. Instead of one small domain in a compact protein, these factors bury one to five divergent homeodomains inside large multidomain proteins, usually alongside many C2H2 zinc fingers: ZHX1-3, ZFHX2 and ZFHX3, HOMEZ, TSHZ1-3, HMBOX1, HDX, HHEX, and the SATB-type CUT-plus-homeodomain proteins. Several were discovered as something else entirely, an AT-rich enhancer-binding protein, a telomere repeat-binding protein, a chromatin scaffold protein. Their motifs are correspondingly heterogeneous: there is no single family consensus, several database models carry almost no information, and where a good motif exists it may be read by the zinc fingers rather than by the homeodomain. Useful as a bucket, not as an identifier.
long:
## The factors

What unites these proteins is architecture, not sequence preference. Domain annotation gives the flavour.
ZHX1 and ZHX3 are 873 and 956 residues with five annotated homeobox regions each plus two C2H2 zinc
fingers; ZHX2 has four homeoboxes. ZFHX3, originally named ATBF1, is 3,703 residues carrying four
homeodomains and 23 zinc fingers; ZFHX2 is 2,572 residues with three homeodomains and 12 zinc fingers.
HOMEZ is a 550-residue protein with three homeodomains and a leucine-zipper-like region and no zinc
fingers at all. TSHZ2 and TSHZ3, vertebrate teashirt proteins, have five zinc fingers and a single
homeodomain annotated as atypical. HDX has two homeodomains; HMBOX1 has one, embedded in a POU-like
arrangement. HHEX is the outlier in the other direction, a 270-residue protein with a single homeodomain,
but it homo-oligomerises through a proline-rich region rather than working as a monomer. SATB1 and SATB2
pair a divergent homeodomain with two CUT domains. Several of these proteins were characterised before
anyone called them homeodomain factors: ZFHX3/ATBF1 as the AT-motif binding factor of the human
alpha-fetoprotein enhancer, HMBOX1 as HOT1, a direct double-stranded telomere repeat-binding protein,
SATB1 as a matrix-attachment-region binding protein with "unusual binding site recognition", and ZHX1 as an
NF-Y-interacting repressor.

## The motif

There is no single consensus, and the entry deliberately does not offer one. The three best-supported
models are as follows. HOMEZ, from HT-SELEX, reads TAATCGTTT, about 13 bits: a recognisable TAAT core with
an unusual CGTTT extension, and it is reproduced independently in CIS-BP as TATAATCGTTTT and as a footprint
archetype, so it is probably real. HMBOX1 gives CTAGTTA, equivalently TAACTAG, supported by both in vitro
selection and ChIP; this is a TAAT-like core with an inverted 3' half. Notably it does not resemble the
TTAGGG telomeric repeat that HOT1/HMBOX1 was reported to bind directly, and that discrepancy is not
resolved in the literature. TSHZ2 gives a 15-base CATCAAATGGAATC with high information content and grade A
evidence, and it contains no TAAT core whatever; the most economical reading is that the zinc fingers do
the binding, as they do for *Drosophila* teashirt, and the atypical homeodomain contributes little. The
remaining models are close to empty: ZFHX2 is a bare TAATTA at 5.5 bits, ZFHX3 reduces to AAT at 2.5 bits,
HHEX to AT at 1.9, ZHX1 to AC at 1.3, HDX to a single T. Family cohesion is 0.55, the lowest of the
homeodomain groups, which is the expected signature of a bucket.

## Where it acts

Genuinely varied, and for several members not well mapped. HMBOX1/HOT1 localises to telomeres and
associates with actively processed telomere ends. ZHX proteins act as promoter-proximal repressors in
complexes with NF-Y. ZFHX3/ATBF1 was defined at an AT-rich enhancer element and binds AT-rich sequence
generally, which is one reason its motif carries so little information. SATB1 occupies base-unpairing
regions and matrix attachment regions and organises chromatin loops in T cells rather than acting at a
short consensus. TSHZ3 works at neuronal target genes in cortical projection neurons. The general pattern
is that occupancy for these proteins is determined by protein-protein interaction and by regional DNA
character, AT-richness or repeat content, more than by a short high-information consensus, which is exactly
why motif-based prediction performs poorly for them.

## Biology and disease

Several members have solid human genetics. Somatic mutation and deletion of ZFHX3/ATBF1 occur recurrently
in prostate cancer. Deletion of TSHZ3 causes an autism syndrome with defects in cortical projection
neurons. De novo mutations in ADNP, another large protein with a homeodomain in unusual company, cause a
SWI/SNF-related autism syndrome. HHEX, as PRH/Hex, is required for formation of the vertebrate body axis,
the haematopoietic and vascular systems, liver, thyroid and forebrain, and it can both repress and activate
targets and additionally regulate nuclear export of specific mRNAs. HMBOX1/HOT1 is a positive regulator of
telomere length: depletion shortens and overexpression lengthens telomeres, and it promotes chromatin
association of telomerase. SATB1 controls thymocyte development through higher-order chromatin
organisation.

## Reading a hit

This is the family where a motif hit licenses the least. Of the 13 models, five carry under 6 bits and
three carry under 3 bits, which means they cannot be scanned meaningfully at all; a "hit" for the CIS-BP
ZHX1 or HDX model is not information. The CIS-BP HHEX model is inherited across species: it was measured on
a *Caenorhabditis elegans* protein at 77% DNA-binding-domain identity and transferred to human HHEX, not
measured on the human protein. The CIS-BP ZFHX2 model is a bare TAATTA whose nearest neighbours across all
four databases are Q50 homeodomain motifs, and the ZHX1 model's nearest neighbours are CpG-binding
MBD/CXXC motifs; both are flagged in the underlying data as probably belonging elsewhere. Only HOMEZ,
HMBOX1 and TSHZ2 rest on direct in vitro selection for the human protein, and for TSHZ2 the motif is
probably the zinc fingers' rather than the homeodomain's. Read a hit here as a statement about sequence
composition, and go to expression and ChIP data before naming a protein.
caveats: Treat this family as a bucket label, not an identification. Five of the 13 models carry under 6 bits and three under 3 bits, so they are not scannable; matches to them are noise. The CIS-BP HHEX model is transferred from a C. elegans protein at 77% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured on human HHEX. The CIS-BP ZFHX2 and ZHX1 models sit closer to Q50 homeodomain and MBD/CXXC motifs respectively than to anything in this family. Only HOMEZ, HMBOX1 and TSHZ2 have credible human in vitro motifs, and the TSHZ2 site contains no TAAT core and is likely read by its zinc fingers. For most members, occupancy is driven by partners and by AT-rich or repeat context, not by the consensus.
